_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — copy to mcpconfig.<env>.json (e.g. mcpconfig.dev.json) and delete this key. `frontmai-cli deployMcpTool` reads mcpconfig.<env>.json for the ACTIVE profile's env, so this .example file is never deployed by accident. Generate the real file with `npx frontmai-cli initMcpTool` (it scaffolds the same fields, all empty) or copy this one. One file per tool: deployMcpTool reads exactly one per directory, so to register a second tool against the same bot, swap this file's contents and re-run it.
_comment_name: Shown to MCP clients in tools/list. MUST match /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ — letters, digits, hyphen, underscore only; no spaces, dots or slashes. Convention: <bot>-<action>.
name: example-tool-action
_comment_description: One line. This is what an MCP client shows the model when deciding whether to call the tool — write it for that reader.
description: One-line summary of what this tool does and when to call it.
_comment_inputSchema: JSON-schema subset. Each properties.<x>.type MUST be one of: string, boolean, number, double. Nothing else is validated by the MCP server; unsupported types default to string.
_comment_enabled: false hides the tool from tools/list and makes tools/call reject it. This is the only documented way to retire a tool — see README § 'Open questions'.
_comment_intentId: MUST equal the INTENT_NAME constant in your tool intent file (src/mcp/<your-tool>.js). A mismatch fails at dispatch, not at deploy.
_comment_botId: MUST equal the botId in deployment.config.<env>.json — same bot, same value. Where a NEW botId comes from is undocumented; ask the platform owner.
_comment_domain: The userDomain the bot lives under. You need the `developer` role on it.
